gaps.term: why the outer two updates are linear
gaps.quote: The outer two cost linear time.
gaps.note: The page does not say why D<-D-H and D<-H-D cost only linear time on the tapes while H<-H+D needs the whole recursive network; the reader cannot check this asymmetry from what is given.

gaps.term: explicit network values W_b and s_b
gaps.quote: the paper's explicit network has $W=W_{\rm b}$ and $s=s_{\rm b}$ (cited)
gaps.note: The cited claim gives no values for W_b and s_b and never describes the explicit network, so its content is empty for the reader and it is not said how it bears on s<W mu.

gaps.quote: At depth $d$, the $s$ smaller calls are interchanges of width $\mu^{d-1}$ on streams of volume $V/W$, which costs $(s/W)F_{d-1}$ per unit volume.
gaps.note: The page defines mu only as the number of rows of a vertex matrix and never explains how a width-mu^d field is split into mu chunks, nor why each smaller call is an interchange of width mu^(d-1) rather than a shear.
Nothing on the page states or cites that mu < 2^20 for the explicit network; the reader cannot check the premise the saving argument rests on.

gaps.term: widths that are not powers of mu
gaps.quote: which for width $u=\mu^d$ is $O(u^{\tau})$ per unit volume
gaps.note: The derivation covers only u = mu^d, while the claimed cost O(V u^tau) is for any u-bit fields; the page does not say how other widths are handled or why padding keeps the bound.

gaps.quote: The shear is such an invocation, with $D$ as $X$ and $H$ as $Y$, so it is exact for any initial auxiliary contents.
gaps.note: The page never says the bit network carrying the shear has banks X and Y indexed by triples S, nor how adding x_S into y_S for each S realises the address update H<-H+D on u-bit fields with entries in Z/qZ.

gaps.quote: A forward, inverse, forward schedule of these invocations exchanges the two banks and returns every auxiliary wire to its starting value (cited).
